text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 5: In the screening months no arm clearly beat B0, though AN had the lowest error'
text.tspan: Figure 5: In the screening months no arm clearly beat B0, though AN had
the lowest error

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'A screen, not a test: the 95% intervals of the arms overlap B0's, so no arm is shown to beat B0. Top: mean absolute error of each arm at lead-day 1 (the forecast for the day after the day it is issued) over the first 10 of the 18 scored months. Orange line: B0's error. Grey bars need no fit. Blue bars are XGBoost models fitted per plant, out-of-fold (each made by a model that never trained on that month), with three training runs (seeds). Bottom: R4 and R5 are scored on CRPS, the continuous ranked probability score, which compares the whole forecast distribution with the measured power. Each is drawn beside B0 on the same rows, with one training run. All rows are exploratory. No pairwise comparison is made here. Arms. AN: the analogue ensemble, the power on the 5 recent days whose forecast clear-sky index (the forecast's irradiance relative to clear sky) was closest to the target day's. R1s: B0 rescaled by the last 7 days' observed over predicted energy, with no fit. Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of the same hour. W7: the minimum, maximum, and mean of the same hour over the last 7 whole days. PC: the ratio of power to the satellite irradiance of the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS). TF: the 30-day ratio of power to forecast irradiance (the transfer ratio). B0: the baseline with no lag. N1: a random day 8 to 28 days earlier (keeps the plant's slowly changing output level). T1: days since the record began. Month-block folds interleave, so trees can interpolate a scored month's level from months on both sides; its gain is what interpolation buys, never drift a live forecast could use. R4: B0 clamped at the plant's clipping ceiling, with no fit. IM: the morning's power on the forecast day. N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null control). L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). KS: all of L1, IM, W7, Q30, TF, S3, and RP together. L2: L1 plus that hour's weather forecast. RP: the plant's recent energy relative to the other plants. S2: a two-step forecast that adds a first-stage forecast and its residual at the lag hour. CK: the plant's clipping ceiling. CTX7: seven separate daily lags and their weather forecasts. S3: a two-step forecast that adds the first-stage forecast's mean residual over the last 1, 7, and 30 days. R2: B0 rescaled by the last 30 days' observed over predicted energy per clock hour, with no fit. climatology: the median power of the plant's calendar month and hour, from months outside the scored block, with no fit. diurnal_persistence: the power at the target's hour on the last whole day before the issue day, with no fit. persistence: the last observed hour's power when the forecast was issued, with no fit. R5: B0 plus recent residual quantiles, with no fit.'
text.tspan: A screen, not a test: the 95% intervals of the arms overlap B0's, so no arm is shown to beat B0. Top: mean absolute
error of each arm at lead-day 1 (the forecast for the day after the day it is issued) over the first 10 of the 18
scored months.
Orange line: B0's error. Grey bars need no fit. Blue bars are XGBoost models fitted per plant, out-of-fold (each
made by a model that never trained on that month), with three training runs (seeds).
Bottom: R4 and R5 are scored on CRPS, the continuous ranked probability score, which compares the whole forecast
distribution with the measured power. Each is drawn beside B0 on the same rows, with one training run.
All rows are exploratory. No pairwise comparison is made here.
Arms. AN: the analogue ensemble, the power on the 5 recent days whose forecast clear-sky index (the forecast's
irradiance relative to clear sky) was closest to the target day's. R1s: B0 rescaled by the last 7 days' observed
over predicted energy, with no fit. Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of the same hour. W7: the minimum,
maximum, and mean of the same hour over the last 7 whole days. PC: the ratio of power to the satellite irradiance
of the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS). TF: the 30-day ratio of power to forecast irradiance (the
transfer ratio). B0: the baseline with no lag. N1: a random day 8 to 28 days earlier (keeps the plant's slowly
changing output level). T1: days since the record began. Month-block folds interleave, so trees can interpolate a
scored month's level from months on both sides; its gain is what interpolation buys, never drift a live forecast
could use. R4: B0 clamped at the plant's clipping ceiling, with no fit. IM: the morning's power on the forecast
day. N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null control). L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the
latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). KS: all
of L1, IM, W7, Q30, TF, S3, and RP together. L2: L1 plus that hour's weather forecast. RP: the plant's recent
energy relative to the other plants. S2: a two-step forecast that adds a first-stage forecast and its residual at
the lag hour. CK: the plant's clipping ceiling. CTX7: seven separate daily lags and their weather forecasts. S3: a
two-step forecast that adds the first-stage forecast's mean residual over the last 1, 7, and 30 days. R2: B0
rescaled by the last 30 days' observed over predicted energy per clock hour, with no fit. climatology: the median
power of the plant's calendar month and hour, from months outside the scored block, with no fit.
diurnal_persistence: the power at the target's hour on the last whole day before the issue day, with no fit.
persistence: the last observed hour's power when the forecast was issued, with no fit. R5: B0 plus recent residual
quantiles, with no fit.
